Final settings (config.json):
  batch_size 4
  workers    14
  prefetch   0

Final throughput: 700.0 req/s at p99 199.0 ms (bench.py: "within the 200 ms limit").
Start point: batch_size 8, workers 1, prefetch 0 gave 100.0 req/s at p99 197.2 ms.

How it was found:
- The p99 limit of 200 ms is a wall (SPEC.md: "not negotiable"). It was a hard filter, never a score:
  every setting with p99 above 200 ms was refused, not traded against throughput.
- Exhaustive search with bench.measure over batch_size 1..9, workers 1..29, prefetch 0..39. These ranges
  cover every setting that can stay within 200 ms (batch_size 9 alone gives 215.6 ms; workers above 23 or
  prefetch above 36 break the wall even at the minimum of the other settings).
- 1174 settings stay within the wall. Best five:
    batch 4, workers 14, prefetch 0: 700.0 req/s, p99 199.0 ms   (chosen)
    batch 5, workers 11, prefetch 0: 687.5 req/s, p99 200.0 ms
    batch 4, workers 13, prefetch 1: 676.0 req/s, p99 197.3 ms
    batch 4, workers 12, prefetch 3: 672.0 req/s, p99 199.7 ms
    batch 5, workers 10, prefetch 1: 650.0 req/s, p99 198.3 ms
- Margin to the wall: 1.0 ms. bench.py is a deterministic model; real p99 has noise, so 1.0 ms of
  margin may not hold in production. If a safety margin is wanted, that is the owner's call.
